subject: Hearthbridge on-prem edge enclave: networking, node pools, and retention constraints
messages:
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@hearthbridge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@hearthbridge.com
Date: 2027-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Hearthbridge on-prem landing: kickoff and constraints (initial)

Marissa / Redwood team,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. We're planning a small on-prem enclave to run inference for our clinical triage models. High level constraints:
- Single rack at our Austin site (42U), limited to 12 usable U, 80A PDUs available.
- No outbound internet except to allowed IPs via NAT gateway (we will provide CIDRs).
- Customer-managed HSM for key material; policy requires CMEK for model weights and audit trails for all control-plane actions.
- Storage: models live on an encrypted blockstore (replicated across two nodes) with NVMe local cache for hot shards.
- RPO for model artifacts: 1 hour; RTO for inference is 5 minutes (failover to cold standby in another region is acceptable).

Please confirm what minimal cluster topology you'd recommend (control-plane HA, node pools, PV configuration) and the items we'll need to provision on our side (VLAN ranges, BGP peering, firewall rules, cabinet power allocation). I've attached our internal constraints spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Tom
Ops Lead, Hearthbridge Labs
Attachments: hearthbridge-constraints.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@hearthbridge.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-02T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hearthbridge on-prem landing: kickoff and constraints (initial)

Tom — thanks, this is helpful. Quick read and proposed next steps below. Attaching a first-draft topology for discussion (proposed-topo-v1.pdf).

Summary of recommended baseline (minimum):
- Control plane: 3 control-plane nodes (HA) on dedicated VLAN, control-plane network isolated from tenant data plane. External access limited to our admin jump host + your VPN.
- Node pools:
  * infra pool (2 x c4.large-equivalent): for logging, monitoring, CSI controllers, conservative resource assumptions
  * model-inference pool (2-4 x GPU nodes): A100-class or equivalent; dual NVMe per node for local cache
  * worker pool (2 x CPU nodes): batch / pre-processing tasks
- Storage classes: encrypted blockstore (replicated RWO) for persistent model storage; local NVMe as ephemeral ReadWriteOnce for cache. Use WaitForFirstConsumer to bind where possible to respect topology.
- KMS/HSM: Redwood will integrate with your customer-managed HSM via KMIP or PKCS11. We will require a service account and network path to the HSM cluster.
- Network: private peering + static routes. NAT egress only through a controlled gateway; list of outbound FQDNs/ips will be provided. BGP for failover to secondary site is supported but optional.
- Observability & audit: we will ship control-plane events to Redwood Console with a read-only viewer for your auditors; audit logs retained 90 days by default (can extend).

Open questions for you:
1) Do you have a preference on in-rack switch model or will we design around IP addressing only?
2) Are we allowed to run internal DNS for service discovery or must we use static entries?
3) Who is the network contact for the VLAN/CIDR and firewall configs?

Next steps: internal technical sync (Redwood) today at 4pm PT; customer network handoff call Tue 11/4 to collect VLANs and firewall rules. If that works we'll send a SOW draft for sign-off.

—Marissa
Director, On-Prem Deployments
Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed-topo-v1.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-02T13:26:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hearthbridge on-prem landing: kickoff and constraints (initial) — tech notes

Folks — notes from my read of their constraints and what I'd recommend from an engineering standpoint. Adding some numbers so procurement can size hardware: 

Control plane:
- 3x small control nodes (8 vCPU, 32GB RAM) with dedicated etcd storage on mirrored NVMe. Keep control-plane on separate VLAN; kube-apiserver load-balanced by local VIP.

Inference node pool sizing (initial):
- 2x A100-similar GPU nodes (80GB GPU memory) if they expect large batch/low-latency model runs. If they want denser smaller-model footprint, we can do 4x T4-class nodes. Start conservative with 2x A100s and a plan to add 1 node after 2 weeks of load testing.
- Node filesystem: each GPU node gets 2x 3.2TB NVMe devices configured as LVM for fast local cache + 1x 16TB encrypted blockstore volume (replicated) mounted as /models. Use a CSI driver that supports block volumes and encryption context propagation.
- PV binding: WaitForFirstConsumer to ensure scheduler places pods on nodes with local NVMe; set reclaimPolicy=Retain for model volumes to avoid accidental deletion. Snapshot schedule nightly (incremental) with 1h RPO target; coordinate replication with your backup appliance.

Networking:
- Recommend enabling NodeLocal DNSCache and CNI with host-local IPAM to avoid ARP storms; static route entries for the HSM IPs and the NAT gateway.
- Firewall: allow inbound from our admin jump host / your org's maintenance IPs to control-plane API port 6443; all other access via bastion + mTLS.

IO/Perf expectations:
- If you expect sustained 4GB/s model reads on cold start, local NVMe cache should mitigate; provide real test artifact set for preflight.
- Provide target p99 latency for inference so we can tune batching/caching: I recommended 50-100ms p99 for their use-case today.

Attaching a short MD with PV/IO SLAs for ops: pv-io-sla.md

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Hearthbridge on-prem landing: kickoff and constraints (initial) — timeline & network handoff

Tom — looping in the implementation plan and next steps. We will prepare a SOW draft and a network handoff worksheet. Please provide the following by end of week so we can lock hardware and schedule an on-site install window:
- VLAN ranges (management / control / tenant / storage) and any reserved IPs.
- HSM endpoint IP(s) and whether KMIP/PKCS11 is preferred.
- Power per cabinet (we need U and A info per U).
- Acceptable maintenance windows for kernel upgrades and reboots (we prefer a weekly 2-hour window).

Planned timeline (rough):
- 11/04: network handoff call to capture VLANs and firewall rules (30-45m)
- 11/08: SOW/delivery schedule shared (SOW-draft-001.docx attached)
- 11/22: target hardware ship and imaging start (subject to procurement lead times)
- 12/06: on-site racking + initial network bring-up

We will also need a point-of-contact from your network/security team for firewall rule testing and a signed data processing addendum before we begin.

Laura Bennett
Principal Delivery Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: SOW-draft-001.docx
